accepted.evidence: To address this, we introduce OV3D-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark that compares open-vocabulary monocular 3D detectors under deployment-realistic conditions across seven indoor and outdoor datasets.

accepted.name: LiveHouse-TS
accepted.evidence: To bridge this gap, we introduce LiveHouse-TS, the first open-world living benchmark infrastructure for TSFMs.

accepted.name: PTXBench
accepted.evidence: We introduce PTXBench, a benchmark for evaluating and adapting large language models (LLMs) to use architecture-specific PTX for GPU kernel optimization.

accepted.name: CADP-Bench
accepted.evidence: To support this setting, we introduce CADP-Bench, an expert-verified benchmark of full academic pages containing tightly coupled text and multiple SAE types, evaluated through a re-injection compilation protocol.

accepted.name: HarnessRisk
accepted.evidence: We present HarnessRisk, a lifecycle oriented benchmark that organizes agent harness safety into six operational phases including Harness Configuration, Capability Extension, Runtime Operation, State Persistence, Action Control, and Incident Recovery.

accepted.name: LIBERO-VIFO
accepted.evidence: To address these gaps, we introduce LIBERO-VIFO, a benchmark to evaluate both the capability and safety of visual cue following in VLA models.

accepted.name: PathoArgus-Bench
accepted.evidence: We introduce PathoArgus-Bench, a benchmark and evaluation protocol that explicitly tests the full evidence chain: availability, accessibility, use, and responsiveness.

accepted.name: MobileWorldSafety
accepted.evidence: To address this gap, we introduce MobileWorldSafety, a benchmark of 142 risk tasks built on real Android applications.

accepted.name: StartupBench
accepted.evidence: We introduce \textbf{StartupBench}, an E2E agent benchmark grounded in market-validated AI startup products.

accepted.name: BEAR-Bench
accepted.evidence: To address these limitations, we introduce BEAR-Bench (Bilingual Enterprise and Academic Reasoning), a self-contained, complex English-and-Russian benchmark comprising 1000 human-annotated questions based on text-rich business and scientific documents.

accepted.name: PRISM
accepted.evidence: In contrast to datasets collected in household or laboratory settings, PRISM provides a realistic benchmark for multimodal perception and control under high-precision industrial constraints, and serves as a foundation for contact-rich, generalizable manipulation in real-world manufacturing environments.
